sentences.text: Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for the State and respondent No.2./party-in-person.

3. The case of the prosecution is that on the first information given by the victim aged about 16 years on NC: 2023:KHC-K:8602 03.01.2023, the police registered FIR against the petitioner for the aforementioned offences.
It is alleged by her that for last one year the accused was teasing her and following her.

On 01.01.2023 at about 5.30 a.m., when she went outside for attending nature's call,
the accused followed her and dragged her and forcefully committed sexual assault, by making her fall down on the floor.
Immediately, she came to the house and as her father was suffering from a paralytic stroke and she felt that not to intimate the family.
But after that she was very sad, the family enquired her and then she revealed the incident.
Immediately they intimated to the neigbours and relatives, then they went to the police station and lodged the complaint.
After registering the FIR, the police arrested this petitioner on 05.01.2023 and he was remanded to judicial custody.
The bail petition of this petitioner was rejected by the Session judge, hence he is before this court.

sentences.text: 2 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended he is innocent of the alleged offence, he has been falsely implicated.
The medical test report does not reveal any sexual assault.
The FSL report also reveals, there is no seminal stains or blood stains, Therefore, he has been falsely implicated.
He is in custody for almost 10 months.
The charge sheet has been filed.
He is ready to abide by any conditions.
Hence, prayed for granting bail.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP seriously objected bail petition and contended that the incident occurred on 01.01.2023.
The complaint was lodged on 03.01.2023 and on 04.01.2023 medical examination was conducted.
The question of detecting the seminal stains does not arises, it may be vanished.
But the statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and the medical report reveals she was sexually assaulted by the accused.
If the petitioner is granted bail, he may tamper the prosecution witnesses and threaten the witnesses, which is not ruled out.
Hence, prayed for rejecting the bail petition.
The father of the victim, the defacto complainant/respondent No.2, appeared and orally objects and submits that the accused sexually abused his daughter and he should not be granted bail.
7. Having heard the arguments, perused the records, on perusal of the same, the complaint came to be registered by the police on the very statement made by the victim girl, aged about 16 years.
She has stated the accused always used to follow her and tease her.
She was unable to intimate the house because of the prestige issue of the family and also her father is also suffering from paralytic disease.
Therefore, she suppressed the matter.

However, on 1.1.2023 at 5.30 a.m., the accused followed her when she went outside of the house for attending the nature's call, at that time he dragged her forcefully and made her to fall down on the ground and sexually assaulted her by force.
The accused said to be threatened her.
She came to the house, but due to fear and thinking that her father may suffer any shock, therefore she has NC: 2023:KHC-K:8602 not informed him immediately.
However, her parents found she was in sad mood and they enquired her.
Subsequently, she has revealed the offence committed by the accused on her.
Subsequently she has intimated to one of the relative Siddappa.
Thereafter, they went to the police station and lodged the complaint .
8. After registering FIR the accused was arrested and remanded to judicial custody.
The victim was subjected to medical examination, where it was revealed the hymen of the victim was not intact which suggests, she was subject to the sexual assault.
The victim is minor aged about 16 years.
Even if there was her willing and consent, which is immaterial.

Though the FSL report reveals there is no semen stains found on the vaginal swab, as contended by the learned HCGP, the medical examination was conducted after 4 days of the incident and meanwhile she had bathed and cleaned the vagina.
Therefore, the question of finding the spermatozoa cannot be expected and it could have been vanished.

The medical NC: 2023:KHC-K:8602 examination report was conducted on 04.01.2023 and thereafter the Investigating Officer also taken the victim to the Magistrate and got recorded the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. where she has categorically stated, the victim was going outside the house to attend nature's call, the accused followed her.

When she was found alone,
he has forcibly committed sexual assault on her.

Considering the statement of the victim both under Mounesh vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171797692/
3 Sections 154 and 164 of Cr.P.C. and the medical examination report, there is a prima facie material for having committed sexual assault on the victim girl.

That apart, if the petitioner is granted bail,
there is every possibility of tampering and threatening the witnesses, which is not ruled out.
Therefore, I am of the view, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
Accordingly bail petition filed by the petitioner/accused is hereby dismissed.
